body:
WinB cargo budget (Opus2, integration owner and scheduler for both projects; set 2026-11-26 ~21:50Z after Greg's „powtorze jeszcze raz, chcialbym przeniesc wiekszosc pracy na Windows B kodwanie, testy itp”, relayed by Fable2 #8105 and Engram::Fable #1886). Capacity from WinB session-5's read-only WMI/CIM report #1499 (21:48Z): 24 logical cores, 103 GB RAM (69 GiB free), FreeVirtualMemory 77 GiB, 323 GB free on C:.
RULES (TermAl and Engram COMBINED on WinB):
1. At most TWO concurrent cargo or launcher test runs on WinB, each with its own worktree and target dir, each capped at CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 (-j2 or less).
2. At most ONE FULL gate on WinB at a time (either project). While a FULL runs, at most ONE other bounded (-j2) run beside it.
3. Launch floor: WinB FreeVirtualMemory >= 20,971,520 KiB, read by the runner at launch. Below it, do not start; tell Opus2.
4. Every WinB cargo or launcher run sends START and END to Opus2. Opus2 grants each by name (a standing grant may cover a session's serial runs on one item). Review and evaluator children on WinB count against memory, not cargo slots.
5. Kill nothing; no process listing (FV/disk census only).
WinB has no Kimi: a Claude refusal on a WinB pair moves that round's pair to Central with Kimi (Fable2 #8105).

SLOT SPLIT (rev 2, added by Opus2 at 2026-11-26 ~22:00Z on Fable2 #8111; source: Engram::Fable #8945, agreed with Termal::Fable2), inside the rules above:
- One bounded -j2 run PER PROJECT at a time (TermAl one, Engram one).
- The single FULL slot alternates between the projects by request time; at most one other bounded run beside a FULL.
- Engram::Fable-WinB (WinB session-24, Engram's WinB coordinator) and Termal::Coord-WinB (WinB session-26, Codex) mail each other START and END for every cargo run and FULL.
- Whoever starts a run checks the FV floor (20,971,520 KiB) at launch.
- Disputes go to Engram::Fable and Termal::Fable2.
- WinB grants MOVE to the two WinB coordinators once Termal::Coord-WinB is briefed by Fable2. Until then Opus2 keeps granting on WinB for both projects, so nothing stalls.

CORRECTION (rev 3, Opus2 ~22:10Z): Engram::Fable-WinB is WinB session-27 (relay-principal-546d7f4c…), not session-24. It introduced itself to Opus2 as session-27; session-24 was a number given in Kimi::Consultant's #75. Termal::Coord-WinB is WinB session-26 (Codex), briefed by Fable2 at about 21:57Z (#8113). The take-over of WinB grants takes effect when Coord-WinB confirms it explicitly to Opus2.

TEMPORARY EXCEPTION (rev 4, Fable2, 2026-11-26 ~22:40Z, ruling on Engram::Fable #8949, which asked for it): Engram's WinB bounded slot was held by a stalled test, test-eb00a39e (Coder4, a 20,000-note fixture, no output since 22:14:43Z). The launcher stop was refused (no supervisor), and nobody kills.
- While test-eb00a39e stays stalled, it does not count against Engram's slot or the "one beside a FULL" count.
- Engram may run ONE new bounded -j2 run in that slot: w-bd4b R15, then w-b07e.
- The stalled run still counts against memory, so the FV floor is checked at every launch by every runner.
- TermAl's slot and the FULL alternation are unchanged. START/END is unchanged.
- The exception ENDS when test-eb00a39e ends; rev 3 applies again in full.
- Coord-WinB was told (relay seq 8). Engram is to file the stall as a defect.
- If the run is still stalled at the next quiet moment, ending it is Greg's act, requested through Asistant.

REV 5 (in force since 2026-11-26 ~22:41Z; supersedes rules 1, 2 and the slot split above). Prompted by Greg's word relayed by Asistant (588693a8 #2892): 'Uzgodnijcie z lokalnym koordynatorem Engram wykorzystanie 96 GB RAM'. Proposed by Fable2 (ebe242f7 #8952); Engram::Fable concurred as written (#8954).
- Per project: up to TWO bounded runs at once, each CARGO_BUILD_JOBS<=4.
- At most ONE FULL per project at a time, so up to two FULLs on WinB.
- At most 4 runs on WinB in total (16 of 24 cores).
- The FV floor of 20,971,520 KiB is read at EVERY launch; below it, wait for an END.
- START/END mail between Coord-WinB (session-26) and Fable-WinB (session-27) is unchanged.
- No kills, no process listings.
- Rev 4's stalled-run exception stays until test-eb00a39e ends. That run was slow quadratic fixture setup, not a hang (Engram w-3b36da2305c7).

REV 6 (in force since 2026-11-26 ~22:45Z; NARROWS rev 5). This is Fable-WinB's counter (WinB relay #8), accepted by Fable2. Greg asked us to agree the RAM use with the LOCAL Engram coordinator, and the counter is the safer of the two.
- Per project: up to TWO bounded runs at once, each CARGO_BUILD_JOBS<=2 (not 4).
- ONE FULL on WinB at a time, host-wide, alternating by request time.
- At most 4 runs on WinB in total.
- The FV floor of 20,971,520 KiB is read at EVERY launch.
- Step-up rule: Coord-WinB and Fable-WinB record the measured FV and commit charge at each START and END. Before raising the job count or allowing two FULLs at once, they review those peaks and agree, telling both central coordinators.
- Rev 4's stalled-run exception stays until test-eb00a39e ends. Its stop was refused by Engram scripts/launcher-stop.mjs:123-126 ('run has no owned Windows job or POSIX process-group supervisor'); the run is letting itself finish, heartbeat active at 22:40:38Z.

CAPACITY CORRECTION (rev 7, Fable2, 2026-11-26 ~22:45Z). Greg's word, relayed by Asistant (588693a8 #2898): '12 corów jest.. 96gb pamięci'. WinB has 12 PHYSICAL cores (24 logical threads) and 96 GB RAM. The "24 cores" figure above counted logical threads; plans must not call them cores.
Rev 6 stays as it is: at most 4 runs x CARGO_BUILD_JOBS<=2 = 8 compile jobs on 12 physical cores, leaving about 4 for the host, agents and evaluators. One FULL host-wide; the FV floor at every launch.
Note for the step-up review: test execution is not covered by CARGO_BUILD_JOBS. Test harnesses default to one thread per logical CPU, so concurrent test phases can oversubscribe. The WinB coordinators also record wall time per stage and watch for slowdowns. A change to test thread counts is a separate decision that must not change test semantics.
